correctness.rationale: Divide the signed transport by strictly positive K(Q) exp(-beta Q), reduce to H(Q)-b, classify using H strictly convex with monotone derivative. The two-positive-crossing window and every equality boundary are proved. Cramer inversion has positive determinant; converse realizability is proven by strict convexity. Third-order Taylor expansion at the minimum gives the fold laws and equal-gap symmetry follows from cosh. Python checker passed 5000 phase tests, 212 inverse tests, exact witness and five fold checks; code is corroboration, not proof.

Jameson supplies the generic zero-count bound, which would cover only the at-most-two component, not the stated exact window and relative-amplitude recovery without further derivation. The other source records concern unrelated objects, different observable maps or different input parameters. Recovery of a signed mixture from its full function is a stronger information regime than recovery from only two zero locations; the 1996 abstract does not imply the latter. The inaccessible full paper is explicitly retained as an unresolved but nondecisive priority risk.

value.rationale: Salt overspill is governed, in the relevant small-transport regime, by independent-channel salinity differences. The natural monitoring question is whether observing two directional changes with varying discharge can identify competing salt pathways without direct salinity amplitude measurement. A sharp three-path necessity/window, exact sign-only inverse, all-pairs realizability and fold ill-conditioning form a complete minimal-model classification useful as an idealized benchmark. It is not an arbitrary numerical slice, a basic zero-count renaming, or a field-calibrated management claim.
